meta.subtitle: Two layers only — a well-known system-level config dir + per-project glossaries. No community registry.
meta.summary: Replace the bundled-in-kit glossary model with a two-layer setup: system-level (~/.config/html-doc/) shared across all projects, plus per-project glossaries. The existing kit-bundled domain files stay git-tracked in this repo as a personal-config backup, not as a runtime source.

blocks.summary: Two layers, no more: a well-known system-level config dir for the user's personal vocabulary, and per-project glossaries next to kit.json. The runtime loader reads from those two places, in that order. The existing kit/glossary/*.json files in this repo stay git-tracked as a backup of the user's personal config — they're no longer auto-loaded as ‘kit bundled defaults’.
bullets: System layer: ~/.config/html-doc/{glossary,extrefs}/*.json — loaded on every page, every project.
Project layer: kit.json + glossary/ alongside it — overrides system on key collision.
Bundled-in-this-repo: kit/glossary/*.json stays for git history + personal backup. NOT auto-loaded.
Drop: community pack registry, packs[] URL list, runtime fetching from CDNs.
Install path: copy/symlink kit/glossary/ → ~/.config/html-doc/glossary/ on dev setup.

blocks.title: What changed from the previous draft
blocks.lead: User feedback collapsed the design. Recording the revisions side-by-side.

cards.title: Dropped — community pack registry
items: No packs[] URL list in kit.json.
No runtime fetch from CDNs / GitHub raw URLs.
No registry index, no html-doc search-packs CLI.
Reason: the user doesn't plan to use it. Scope-creep with no consumer.

cards.title: Kept + refined — two layers
items: System: well-known per-user config directory.
Project: glossary files alongside kit.json (already supported).
Loader merges system then project; project wins on key collision.
Reason: clean, predictable, no network at runtime.

cards.title: New — bundled files stay in repo
items: kit/glossary/*.json + kit/extrefs/*.json keep their git history.
Reframed from ‘kit-shipped runtime defaults’ to ‘personal-config backup’.
Optional install step copies (or symlinks) them into ~/.config/html-doc/.
Reason: user wants the version history and portability, just not the runtime coupling.

blocks.title: Two layers, at a glance
blocks.lead: Each layer answers a different scope question. The runtime loader merges them in order.

rows: Every project on this user's machine
Every page render of this project

blocks.title: Why ‘system’, not ‘global’
blocks.content: ‘global’ implies machine-wide / multi-user. The dir is per-user (under HOME). Calling it ‘system’ makes the analogy with .gitconfig / .npmrc — anything in ~/.config/html-doc/ is the user's personal default for every html-doc project they touch.

blocks.title: Directory layout after the change
blocks.lead: What lives where, with the personal repo still git-tracked.

blocks.title: Loader sequence
blocks.lead: What chrome.js does on every page render. Project wins on collision.

blocks.caption: Load system first, project second; merge keys with project winning.

<project>/glossary/ participant Reg as Term registry Page->>Chrome: render(page) Chrome->>Sys: GET /_system/glossary/<domain>.json Sys-->>Chrome: terms { ... } Chrome->>Proj: GET ./glossary/<domain>.json Proj-->>Chrome: terms { ... } (optional) Chrome->>Reg: merge(system, project) — project wins Reg-->>Page: tooltips wired

blocks.title: Failure handling
blocks.content: Missing system files: no warning — most projects don't need a personal layer. Missing project files declared in kit.json.domains: surfaced in the existing warning panel with a jump-to-file affordance. No network failure paths to think about — everything is local.

blocks.title: kit.json after the change
blocks.lead: Minimal schema change. The packs[] field never landed; domains[] keeps its current meaning, scoped to the project layer only.

rows: Names of project-level files under <project>/glossary/. System files are loaded automatically and don't need to be listed.
The CDN-pack design is rolled back; this field never ships.

blocks.title: How serve and build resolve the system layer
blocks.lead: Browser code can't read ~/.config. The CLI bridges it.

cards.title: Dev (html-doc serve)
items: Serve mounts ~/.config/html-doc/ at the URL prefix /_system/.
chrome.js fetches /_system/glossary/*.json + ./glossary/*.json — both are HTTP gets.
404s from missing system files are silent (system layer is optional).
No daemon, no watcher needed — system files are re-fetched each page load.

cards.title: Static (html-doc build)
items: Build reads ~/.config/html-doc/ at build time and inlines into the standalone HTML.
Embedded as window.__htmldocSystemGlossary = { ... } in the bootstrap block.
chrome.js prefers inlined data over /_system/ HTTP when present — same code path, different source.
Build artifact is portable to any browser: no local config dependency.

cards.title: Site build (dist/site/)
items: Multi-page HTTP site — chrome.js fetches /_system/glossary/*.json once per session.
Build copies the resolved system layer into dist/site/_system/ at build time.
Same kit code path as dev; just static files behind the same URL prefix.

cards.title: Personal-repo install
items: Add html-doc install-system command: symlinks (or copies) kit/glossary/ + kit/extrefs/ from this repo into ~/.config/html-doc/.
Symlink keeps git tracking live — edits in the repo are reflected immediately in every project.
Copy is for users who clone this repo on a different machine and don't want a symlink.

blocks.title: Migration phases
blocks.lead: Each step independently ships; stop after any one if the next isn't worth doing.

steps.title: Add the system-layer loader
steps.content: chrome.js fetches /_system/glossary/*.json + /_system/extrefs/*.json before the project layer. html-doc serve mounts ~/.config/html-doc/ at /_system/ with a 404-is-silent policy. No project changes required.

steps.title: Drop the kit-bundled runtime path
steps.content: Stop fetching from _kit/glossary/ at runtime. The repo's kit/glossary/*.json files remain in git but are no longer URL-served as runtime glossary sources. Update tests that assumed the kit path.

steps.title: Add html-doc install-system
steps.content: Subcommand that copies or symlinks kit/glossary/ + kit/extrefs/ into ~/.config/html-doc/. Defaults to symlink when the source is the in-repo path (the maintainer's case); copy for everyone else. Idempotent.

steps.title: Build-time inlining
steps.content: html-doc build reads ~/.config/html-doc/ and inlines it into the standalone HTML. chrome.js prefers inlined data when present. Distinguish a missing system layer (silent) from a present-but-empty one (no inline emitted).

rows: Yes — fall back to ~/.config/html-doc/ if unset.

What if the user has two unrelated personal vocabularies?
Keep both in ~/.config/html-doc/ under different domain filenames.
